newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, AGAs seen neutral.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, AGAs seen neutral.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, pressured early by softer physical prices, ended lower Wednesday in thin trade, then showed little reaction in the after-hours ACCESS session following neutral AGA data.

May slipped 1.5 cents to close at $1.901 per million British thermal units, then eased only slightly on ACCESS after the weekly stock report. June settled 0.7 cent lower at $1.97. Other deferreds ended down by 0.2 to 2.8 cents.
"The AGAs were at the upper end of the range, but I don't think it's enough to get real bearish about. A lot of people anticipated the first build," said Chris Bray at United Fuels.

AGA said late Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 21 bcf, the first build of the injection season. The gain was slightly above expectations and edged inventories to 293 bcf, or 52 percent, above year-ago. Eastern storage climbed to 205 bcf above last year, more than double 1996 levels.

Traders said reports of softer physical prices helped undermine the complex today. While growing inventories should limit any upside, they said favorable spreads still encouraged up front buying and should temper the bears.
Technical traders said recent ranges were still intact, with May support still in the $1.825-1.85 area and resistance at $2, then at $2.045-2.05 and $2.10.
Six- to 10-day forecasts are still calling for below-normal temperatures for the eastern two-thirds of the nation, with the West expected to stay above-normal.

In Wednesday's cash, Gulf Coast prices fell by a few cents to the low-to-mid $1.90s. Midcontinent pipes were down a similar amount to the low-to-mid $1.80s. Gas at the New York city gate was mostly talked in the low-to-mid $2.40s, up more than five cents on the day.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip fell 0.7 cent to $2.107. NYMEX said 29,013 Hub contracts traded, little changed from Tuesday's revised tally of 29,790.
No Permian or Alberta natgas futures traded Wednesday.
On the KCBT, May finished one cent higher at $1.77, while deferreds ended narrowly mixed. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.5 cents to 13.1 cents (NYMEX premium).
